title: Why Your Enterprise Tech Stack Isn’t Ready for AI Agents — Christopher Lovejoy & Saul Howard
talk_summary: Anthropic FDE and Anterior VP describe four architectural primitives for production agents in regulated enterprises: an immutable event log of every agent action, schema-driven object storage separated from orchestration, human/LLM action equivalence for escalation, and evals that fall out of replaying the ledger. The core argument is to design for auditability, data isolation, escalation, and replay from day one rather than bolting them onto a demo.

takeaways.technique: Immutable append-only event ledger as source of truth
takeaways.what_they_do: All agent actions are written as timestamped, append-only events; system state is a computed projection, so any point in time can be reconstructed and replayed.

takeaways.technique: Replay-based evals from the action ledger
takeaways.what_they_do: Because every action and its full context is recorded, they replay a historical point, tweak prompt/model/code, and measure the direct impact; human-vs-agent output on the same task is the eval score.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can go back to any particular time ... you could tweak a prompt, you could tweak a model, you could tweak the code, and you can see the exact direct impact

takeaways.what_they_do: Platform treats humans and LLMs as the same kind of actor, so any action an agent can take a human can take, and downstream steps don't care which one did it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: any action that can be taken by an LLM could also be taken by a human ... any step downstream doesn't care

takeaways.technique: Shared context object rendered per audience
takeaways.what_they_do: Define context once, then map it into an agent-friendly prompt or a human-friendly UI from the same source.
takeaways.evidence_quote: define methods that take the context ... map into something that's agent friendly like a prompt or into something that's more human friendly

takeaways.technique: Separate event log from data blobs; token-scoped access at point of use
takeaways.what_they_do: Events hold only references to immutable, schema-described blobs; agents bear tokens to fetch data at point of use, preventing data flowing freely and limiting prompt-injection blast radius.
